story.value: The name dysprosium comes from the Greek word dysprositos, meaning hard to get at.
French chemist Paul-Émile Lecoq de Boisbaudran discovered dysprosium in 1886, as an impurity in erbia, the oxide of erbium.
Dysprosium was first isolated by the French chemist Georges Urbain in 1906.

uses.value: When combined with vanadium and other rare earth elements, dysprosium is used as a laser material.
A cement made with dysprosium oxide and nickel has been used in cooling nuclear reactor rods.
Compounds called dysprosium-cadmium chalcogenides have been used as sources of infrared radiation for studying chemical reactions.
